summary: North Macedonia's statistics office publishes reported adult perpetrators of every Criminal Code chapter by ethnic affiliation (Macedonian, Albanian, Turkish, Roma, Serb, Bosniak and others), with affiliation unknown for only about 3%. That is real ethnicity data for perpetrators, but by broad chapter rather than child-specific offence, and for reported rather than convicted people. Child victims are counted without ethnicity.
european_title: Ethnic groups are identified; ethnic Europeans as a whole are not a category
european_note: MAKSTAT records ethnic affiliation (Macedonian, Albanian, Turkish, Roma, Vlach, Serb, Bosniak, other), and each named group is shown separately. The source defines no 'ethnic European' category and its 'other' column is mixed, so ethnic Europeans as a whole are not computed. It covers reported adult perpetrators only, by offence chapter.

breakdown.why: MAKSTAT table 105 gives reported adult perpetrators (known offenders) of crimes against sexual freedom and sexual morality in 2025 by ethnic affiliation: 124 in total, 69 Macedonians, 19 Albanians, 15 Turks, 17 Roma, 4 unknown. The chapter mixes child and adult victims; these are reported, not convicted, persons. Child victims of sexual abuse (67 in 2025) have no ethnicity. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Reported adult perpetrators of crimes against marriage, family and youth (519; includes neglect and abuse of a child) by ethnic affiliation: 304 Macedonians, 67 Albanians, 12 Turks, 91 Roma, 9 Serbs, 18 Bosniaks, 5 other, 13 unknown. 229 child victims of domestic violence (2025) have no ethnicity. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Reported adult perpetrators of crimes against life and body (1,150; murders plus bodily injury) by ethnic affiliation: 654 Macedonians, 251 Albanians, 52 Turks, 125 Roma, 38 unknown. All victim ages. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The national commission identified 5 trafficking victims in 2025 (4 children) and 24 presumed victims (17 children); 'the majority were nationals of the country', with no counts. Traffickers fall in the crimes-against-humanity chapter, published by ethnic affiliation as a whole (67 reported adults, 7 unknown). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Child pornography offences are inside the sexual freedom and morality chapter, published by ethnic affiliation only as a whole (124 reported adults, 4 unknown). No victims by ethnicity. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: North Macedonia scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. It records real ethnicity: the statistics office publishes reported adult perpetrators of every Criminal Code chapter by ethnic affiliation (Macedonian, Albanian, Turkish, Roma, Serb, Bosniak and others), with few unknown, so the 25% cap does not apply. Points stay moderate because it covers perpetrators only, by broad chapter rather than child-specific offence, and victims have no ethnicity.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
